what: The control: the first 20 000 replies of the same capture, about 25 minutes of pinging. Everything is held fixed except how long the attacker listened, and no key comes out.

victim.stack: RIOT GNRC at f59dcdace51d34218c24339d299ebc3777ec45bc with ieee802154_security at its defaults (security level 6, ENC-MIC-64, channel 26, PAN 0x0023). No RIOT source change: the key is a CFLAGS define of CONFIG_IEEE802154_SEC_DEFAULT_KEY, built by demos/riot_802154/victim
victim.flash_acr: n/a -- the nRF52840 has no wait-state register and no data cache; the channel is the flash read latch, one 16-byte row
victim.table: RIOT sys/crypto/aes.c Te0, 256 x 4 bytes. The default build has no Te1..Te4: aes.c:149-155 defines all five macros in terms of Te0, so the last round reads this same table

instrument.board: nRF52840 Dongle running instruments/riot802154_stamp, with the wrong link key so it authenticates none of the replies it attacks
instrument.times: reply RADIO END minus request RADIO END, both latched in hardware by PPI channel 18 into TIMER4->TASKS_CAPTURE[0], so no ISR latency is in the number. The MAC ACK interval is recorded too and is used as a common-mode reference

geometry.note: Te0 landed 8 bytes into its 16-byte row in THIS build, so line_off is 2. The campaign's earlier image of the same source had it at 0. Read it off your own ELF with victim/verify_build.py; the control in this json's `control` block is what wrong costs.

attack.expect_note: 2 of 16 round-key bytes from the vote and nothing in the 2^20 candidates the walk tries. A statistic is not a channel.

truth.note: Generated by victim/gen_key.py immediately before the run and compiled into the victim. The recovery never reads it; it is here so the replay can regenerate the blocks and check the answer.

control.holds_fixed: the victim and its build, the attacker, the traffic shape, the row offset, the conditioning and the search. The only thing that changes is the number of replies: 20 000 against 60 000.
control.what_it_does_not_establish: It is a trace-count null, not a structural one. It says this analysis does not manufacture a key out of any capture you hand it. The shuffled-timing and wrong-key controls tools/replay.py --controls prints ARE structural, and so is the row-offset sweep in the other vector's json.

capture.note: 749 of the 80 380 clean replies do not regenerate under the key and are not in the vector. That is the extractor's predicted reply plaintext missing on an odd frame -- an ICMPv6 echo whose 6LoWPAN compression or ICMP body differed -- and not the key. The campaign's own capture had this at 0.09 %; this one at 0.93 %, so expect it to vary with how much other traffic the link carries.
